messages:
Carla M.: Hey team — quick Q about oncall scope for non-incident handoffs. Who owns what between SRE and Runtime for perf regressions, degraded tail latency spikes, and KV cache misses? Also want to clarify escalation path if we see sustained errors >1min but not affecting all customers.
Ben R.: Short: SRE owns infra-level alerts (node, network, infra autoscaling). Runtime owns model-serving-layer, batching logic, and model fallbacks. If you're unsure ping both in #eng-oncall and tag @oncall-sre.
Alice T.: Adding: Runtime will handle model-level rollbacks and model-version fallbacks. We'll also own per-route routing config. SRE can help with capacity/cluster remediation.
Dave (EngMgr): For handoffs please include last 24h error-rate, any recent deploys, PromQL snippet, and whether replay is set. Minimal checklist below.
Carla M.: Can you paste the checklist?
Dave (EngMgr): ```
- deploys -> last successful commit + time
- alert summaries -> graphs + top error codes
- mitigation tried -> rollbacks, scale up
- who to call -> primary oncall + runtime oncall
- docs + runbook links
```
Ben R.: On escalation: if errors affect >10% of requests for >5min -> Severity 2; full outage -> Sev1. If it's a perf tail increase (p95 up but p50 steady) treat as Sev3 unless SLA breach. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall-severity
Eva S.: For handoffs, paste a minimal PromQL you used and any KV cache hit rates. Also tag model owner if model change involved.
Carla M.: OK thanks. One more: if we detect KV cache miss storm causing perf spike but infra looks fine, is that runtime first response? @Ben R.?
Ben R.: Runtime first. SRE will assist if node CPU or networking abnormal. If you're hitting GC or OOMs it's infra.
oncall-bot: Reminder: please update the oncall-handoff doc in Confluence after transfers. Template: https://redwood.internal/confluence/oncall-handoff
Carla M.: I'll update and include the snippets. Thanks :thumbsup:
Alice T.: I'll add a "model-change" checkbox to the template so owners get auto-notified.
Dave (EngMgr): Great. If anyone wants, I'll do a short async doc clarifying boundary cases later today.
Carla M.: Sounds good — marking this resolved for now.
